  "summary": "S1 — Fact: organisers create capacity-limited events and people reserve seats through a small Python HTTP service. Assumptions: POST /events accepts {\"seats\": positive integer} and returns 201 with {\"id\": opaque ID, \"seats_remaining\": integer}; POST /events/{id}/reservations accepts an empty JSON object, reserves one seat, and returns 201 with {\"event_id\": ID, \"seats_remaining\": integer}. Invalid JSON, fields, or capacity return 400; an unknown event returns 404; a full event returns 409; unexpected server failures return 500; errors use {\"error\": string}. The runtime does not identify actors or collect personal details; anyone with access can use either endpoint and see the responses. Event state is shared by all callers of one server process, held in memory, and cleared on restart; reservation updates are serialized to prevent overbooking. These defaults rule out authentication, private event data, persistence, and sharing across server processes. The service binds to localhost:8000 by default. Discovery must first inspect the available workspace and runtime, then establish whether evidence specifies an API contract, identity, persistence, concurrency, deployment, or runtime requirements; it blocks finalizing those choices if evidence contradicts the defaults. Discovery leads, not verified facts: the workspace or team, relevant channels, internal sites and documentation, private repositories, owners, and the meanings of organiser, event, and reservation; no sensitive locator was supplied, and any discovered sensitive locator belongs only in an authorized private store, never KNOWLEDGE/. No deployment target or release authority is named, so the assumed delivery is the returned source checkout. In an isolated run, the original checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; a deployed outcome would exist only after release. S2 — Fact: include tests. Assumptions: standard-library unittest tests exercise the real HTTP boundary, including successful creation and reservation, invalid requests, unknown and full events, and concurrent reservations; run them with python -m unittest discover. Discovery must first inspect the workspace and available Python, then establish whether an existing test convention applies; this blocks finalizing the test command if evidence contradicts the default. This intake implements nothing; the requested service and tests become visible in the returned checkout at final return."
